sets.name: Cloud & identity exposure
sets.description: Six questions written for a cloud/security-platform team: blast radius, egress risk and privilege posture instead of patch priority. Compare it against baseline on the same CVE to see how much of the routing answer is framing.

iam_action.instructions: Choose the identity-side action this finding implies, assuming workload patching proceeds separately.

criteria.rotate-now: Credentials or tokens reachable from this asset could already be compromised: exposed endpoint, remote code execution, or active exploitation reported.
criteria.scope-down: No evidence of compromise, but the role or service is over-privileged for what it does; narrow permissions while the fix ships.
criteria.track: Internal, low-value, no privilege concern implied by the state: record it and move on.
criteria.needs-intel: The state does not reveal what permissions or secrets this workload holds; ask the platform team.

tenant_blast_radius.instructions: What share of the cloud estate becomes reachable once this workload is owned?

criteria.name: single-workload
criteria.description: Compromise stops at this workload; no shared credentials or data path.

criteria.name: single-account
criteria.description: The account or project is affected: other services in the same boundary are exposed.

criteria.name: shared-services
criteria.description: Shared infrastructure such as a TLS terminator, gateway or CI runner sits between this and everything else.

criteria.name: whole-org
criteria.description: Tier-0, internet-exposed and holding payments or PII: an entry point to the organisation.

data_egress_risk.instructions: Rate the risk that data reachable from this asset leaves the estate.

criteria.name: negligible
criteria.description: No sensitive classification and no reachable store worth exfiltrating.

criteria.name: minor
criteria.description: Internal or corporate data only.

criteria.name: significant
criteria.description: PII or business-sensitive records reachable from the workload.

criteria.name: severe
criteria.description: Payment data or regulated records on an internet-exposed service.

publicly_reachable.instructions: Answer yes if an untrusted network can reach this asset as described in the state.

least_privilege_violated.instructions: Answer yes when the asset's role implies it holds broader permissions than its function needs: crown-jewel data plus a shared or platform-level role.

crypto_posture_risk.instructions: Rate the risk that data at rest or in transit on this asset is inadequately protected, judging only from classification and exposure.

criteria.name: none
criteria.description: Nothing sensitive, so protection gaps carry no consequence.

criteria.name: minor
criteria.description: Internal data where weak or undocumented protection would be a quality issue.

criteria.name: moderate
criteria.description: Corporate or customer data with no evidence in the state of encryption at rest.

criteria.name: severe
criteria.description: Payments or PII on an exposed endpoint where transport or storage protection is unknown.

sets.name: Container workload
sets.description: Four questions for Kubernetes and CI estates, where the interesting variable is neighbour risk rather than the CVE.

workload_action.instructions: Pick the workload-level response, assuming the image rebuild happens on its own track.

criteria.cordon-and-patch: Node or cluster escape is plausible on an exposed or privileged workload: drain, rebuild, resume.
criteria.rolling-restart: The fix is a rebuild away and blast radius is small; roll the fleet on schedule.
criteria.backlog: Internal, non-privileged, no shared namespace: a normal backlog item.
criteria.needs-intel: The state does not say whether this workload is privileged or shares a namespace; ask the platform owner.

node_escape_likelihood.instructions: How likely is a compromise of this workload to reach the node or other pods?

criteria.name: theoretical
criteria.description: Unprivileged, isolated, no host paths; escape would need a second bug.

criteria.name: plausible
criteria.description: Shared namespace or broad capabilities make escape conceivable but not easy.

criteria.name: likely
criteria.description: Privileged or host-mounted workload on a reachable node.

criteria.name: observed
criteria.description: The described flaw is remote code execution on an internet-facing tier-0 service.

shared_namespace_risk.instructions: Answer yes if the workload plausibly shares a network or PID namespace with neighbours, so one compromise is many.

image_provenance_risk.instructions: Rate the risk from unclear image provenance for this workload.

criteria.name: signed-pinned
criteria.description: Signed and digest-pinned in a registry with policy enforcement.

criteria.name: signed-only
criteria.description: Signed but moving by tag; a rebuild may pull something different.

criteria.name: unsigned
criteria.description: No signature evidence for a workload running near sensitive data.

criteria.name: unknown
criteria.description: The state says nothing about where this image came from, and the asset matters.
